alerts.title: TDF toxicity: low phosphate, proteinuria, back pain
alerts.message: Guidelines list TDF major toxicity as CKD, AKI, Fanconi syndrome, with lower back pain, bone aches, and muscle cramps as presenting signs; recommended workup includes LFTs and RFTs. Patient on TDF 6 years presents with 4 months of lower back pain and heavy thighs, serum phosphate 0.78 mmol/L, and trace proteinuria. Hypophosphataemia and proteinuria are consistent with TDF-induced proximal tubulopathy. Evidence against drug attribution: creatinine 112 umol/L is within normal limits, and occupational strain from truck driving could explain musculoskeletal symptoms. However, normal creatinine does not exclude early tubular dysfunction, and the combination of low phosphate with proteinuria is a compounding risk. Ibuprofen use adds nephrotoxicity risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate renal tubular function (urine protein-to-creatinine ratio, fractional phosphate excretion). Consider substituting TDF with TAF or AZT if tubulopathy confirmed. Avoid NSAIDs pending evaluation.

alerts.title: Missing TDF renal monitoring per guidelines
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF-containing regimens. Today's creatinine is 112 umol/L but no eGFR was calculated or documented. No prior creatinine values are available to assess trend over 6 years of TDF exposure. Trace proteinuria was noted but attributed solely to hypertension without further renal workup. Given concurrent low serum phosphate and ongoing TDF use, renal monitoring is incomplete.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR, compare with any prior creatinine values, and perform quantitative protein assessment. Schedule renal monitoring at guideline-recommended intervals.

alerts.title: EFV may reduce amlodipine levels, BP uncontrolled
alerts.message: Guidelines state efavirenz can potentially decrease dihydropyridine (amlodipine) drug levels, though no dose adjustments are required. Patient has suboptimal BP control at 146/94 mmHg. The clinician attributes this solely to missed doses, but EFV-mediated induction of CYP3A4 may also lower amlodipine exposure and contribute to inadequate BP control. Trace proteinuria may reflect end-organ damage from persistent hypertension.

evidence.recommended_action: Reinforce amlodipine adherence and recheck BP. If BP remains elevated despite adherence, consider switching antihypertensive or ART regimen. Monitor for target organ damage.

alerts.title: Ibuprofen plus TDF increases renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines identify TDF as a nephrotoxic agent requiring renal monitoring. Patient uses over-the-counter ibuprofen regularly for chronic back pain. Concurrent NSAID and TDF use compounds risk of renal injury, particularly given existing trace proteinuria and low serum phosphate suggesting possible early tubular dysfunction. The clinician's plan recommends PRN ibuprofen without flagging this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Advise limiting ibuprofen use. Consider non-NSAID analgesia for chronic back pain. Monitor renal function and proteinuria closely if NSAID use continues.
